title: Add runtime data/tool reach rule to the reader prompt
summary: Add one concise rule to crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md: when a change reads data or calls a tool at runtime, the reading names the role or process that runs it, what its permissions allow, and whether the data is reachable from there, and puts any limit found into acceptance_criteria. The audience is the reader agent and the verifiers who judge its readings. The reader prompt set has 3 tokens of headroom, so the producer must tighten wording elsewhere in reader.md to stay within 2,000 tokens.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md has a new bullet under 'Reading the request' saying that when a change reads data or calls a tool at runtime, the reading states (1) which role or process runs it, (2) what that runtime may do under its permissions, and (3) whether the data is reachable from there.
The bullet tells the reader to put any limit it finds (unreachable data, denied tool, missing permission) into acceptance_criteria.

Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: the reader prompt set stays within its 2,000-token budget (it has only 3 tokens spare, so other wording in reader.md must be tightened without dropping any existing rule's meaning) and all tests pass. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.

The diff touches only reader.md: no other prompt file, athena.toml (budgets not raised) or defaults.toml changes. The new rule is one or two lines, written for an outside reader, and every original rule in reader.md is still present in meaning, checked with git diff.
